# lagprotest

**lagprotest** extends the Procrustean randomization test (PROTEST) to
ordered multivariate series. It scans Procrustes concordance between two
configurations across candidate temporal lags, tests each lag by
permutation, and returns the lag profile, the lag of maximal concordance
(minimum *m*²), a global p-value that accounts for scanning several lags
and selecting the best one, and per-observation Procrustes residuals.

Three permutation schemes are available:

- `permutation = "phase"` (default): phase-randomized surrogates of `Y`,
  which keep the autocorrelation of each variable and the
  cross-correlations among them. Recommended for the global p-value.
- `permutation = "cyclic"`: cyclic shifts of the full series, optionally
  with its time reversal, applied before lagging. Keeps temporal
  autocorrelation under the null, but the global p-value has low power.
- `permutation = "free"`: free permutation of rows within the
  overlapping window, as in
  [`vegan::protest()`](https://vegandevs.github.io/vegan/reference/procrustes.html).
  Rows are assumed exchangeable, which autocorrelated series violate;
  Type I error can be severely inflated.

## Installation

From [r-universe](https://diogoprov.r-universe.dev/lagprotest):

``` r

install.packages("lagprotest",
                 repos = c("https://diogoprov.r-universe.dev",
                           "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
```

Or the development version from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("diogoprov/lagprotest")
```

## Example

``` r

library(lagprotest)

# Two 12-month series in which X leads Y by 2 months
sim <- simulate_lagged_series(n_times = 12, true_lag = 2, noise_sd = 0.5,
                              seed = 1)

fit <- lagged_protest(sim$X, sim$Y, lags = 0:4, seed = 1)
fit             # optimal lag, global p, effect measures, lag profile
fit$p.global    # p-value of the whole scan, to report for the optimal lag
fit$effect      # effect lag (largest z), Z, A and corrected RV
plot(fit)       # m2 against lag, with the permutation null quantile
residuals(fit)  # per-observation residuals at the optimal lag
```

Report the global p-value (`fit$p.global`) for the optimal lag: it
accounts for scanning several lags and selecting the best one, whereas
the per-lag p-values do not. The continuous measures in `fit$effect`
(`Z`, `A` and the chance-corrected RV coefficient) describe the strength
of the association and, unlike p-values, are not bounded by the number
of permutations.

[`lagged_protest_pairs()`](https://provetelab.org/lagprotest/reference/lagged_protest_pairs.md)
runs the scan on every pair of data sets in a named list and adjusts the
global p-values across pairs. The package includes a real example,
`dminutus_liver` (monthly hepatic and climatic series of a treefrog),
analyzed in the article [Seasonal liver plasticity in a
treefrog](https://provetelab.org/lagprotest/articles/liver-example.html).

Inputs can be matrices or data frames (rows = ordered time points,
columns = variables) or `dist` objects, which are converted to principal
coordinates. See the
[articles](https://provetelab.org/lagprotest/articles/) for choosing a
permutation scheme and simulating series for a calibration study.

## Status

Under development. The method and its calibration are described in a
manuscript in preparation.

# Package index

## Lagged PROTEST

- [`lagged_protest()`](https://provetelab.org/lagprotest/reference/lagged_protest.md)
  : Lagged Procrustean randomization test
- [`plot(`*`<lagged_protest>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/lagprotest/reference/plot.lagged_protest.md)
  : Plot the lag profile of a lagged PROTEST
- [`autoplot(`*`<lagged_protest>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/lagprotest/reference/autoplot.lagged_protest.md)
  : Plot the lag profile of a lagged PROTEST with ggplot2
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<lagged_protest>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/lagprotest/reference/as.data.frame.lagged_protest.md)
  : Lag profile of a lagged PROTEST as a data frame
- [`summary(`*`<lagged_protest>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/lagprotest/reference/summary.lagged_protest.md)
  [`print(`*`<summary.lagged_protest>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/lagprotest/reference/summary.lagged_protest.md)
  : Summarize a lagged PROTEST
- [`residuals(`*`<lagged_protest>`*`)`](https://provetelab.org/lagprotest/reference/residuals.lagged_protest.md)
  : Per-observation Procrustes residuals at the optimal lag
- [`lagged_protest_pairs()`](https://provetelab.org/lagprotest/reference/lagged_protest_pairs.md)
  : Lagged PROTEST for several pairs of data sets

## Simulation

- [`simulate_lagged_series()`](https://provetelab.org/lagprotest/reference/simulate_lagged_series.md)
  : Simulate a pair of multivariate series with a known lag

## Data

- [`dminutus_liver`](https://provetelab.org/lagprotest/reference/dminutus_liver.md)
  :

  Seasonal hepatic and climatic series of *Dendropsophus minutus*

- [`lakewa_blocks()`](https://provetelab.org/lagprotest/reference/lakewa_blocks.md)
  : Lake Washington plankton and limnology blocks
